static_leakage_w_per_mm2_logic.note: 0.06 W per mm2 of STANDARD-CELL (logic) region at a 7 nm-class node, at 0.70-0.75 V and 85-105 C junction, on a mix weighted toward RVT. THE UNIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS THE SUBMISSION'S worst defect: it is per mm2 of standard-cell region, NOT per mm2 of die, so on a part that is mostly array this term is charged over the logic only. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 2x UP from the submitted 0.03. The chain is: an executed ASAP7 place-and-route base of 0.74e-3 W/mm2 of 100%-filled cell area at 25 C/0.70 V typical (from this repository's own results/physical_abi3/asap7 metadata, cross-checked three ways against the liberty's 1 pW leakage unit and against real-scale ASAP7 cell areas), times a threshold-flavour mix, a temperature factor and a voltage factor. The correction is in the threshold ladder: the submission put RELATIVE per-flavour offsets (SLVT 0, LVT 0.071, RVT 0.142 V) inside an exponential that needs the ABSOLUTE saturation threshold, and a device with Vth = 0 is not off. That ladder predicts a 25->100 C ratio of 12.69x at typical/nominal, which is BELOW the 13.82x ASAP7's own SS liberty measures at a slower process AND a lower voltage -- impossible. Re-anchoring to absolute Vth_sat (RVT 0.24, LVT 0.169, SLVT 0.098 V, the lowest ladder clearing that floor) moves the combined mix x T x V factor from 14.8 to 25.3 at the low end and 62.4 to 114.8 at the point. The submission's structural claim that leakier flavours scale less steeply, so mix and temperature partly cancel, is separately FALSIFIED by the same library: measured INVx1 FF/TT ratios are 0.638 / 0.546 / 0.646 across RVT/LVT/SLVT -- flat and non-monotonic -- where the model needs a 1.5x spread. The high end 0.20 is CAPPED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE CHAIN: the chain's own 40/40/20 mix at 105 C and 0.85 V gives 0.43 W/mm2, which is 86% of thermal.cooling_limit_w_per_mm2 and is not physical for a shipping part; 0.19-0.20 is where an A100 lands at ~39% of TDP, the top of ReGate's measured 30-72% static-power band. Grade stays `assumed` and correctly so: ASAP7 is a predictive academic PDK, no datacentre die's Vt mix is published anywhere, and the absolute threshold ladder is inferred from Ioff-per-micron rather than read off a datasheet. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a foundry N7/N6 leakage-per-mm2 figure at a stated PVT, or an ASAP7 SRAM-flavour and LVT/SLVT SS liberty.
static_leakage_w_per_mm2_logic.source: ASAP7 7.5-track predictive PDK NLDM libraries (RVT/LVT/SLVT TT and SS corners) and this repository's executed ASAP7 place-and-route leakage at results/physical_abi3/asap7/add_bf16_sram_engine/pnr_artifacts/metadata.json ; ReGate, MICRO 2025, arXiv:2508.02536, which reports static power at 30-72% of NPU energy

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_rom_array.note: 6.7e-3 W per mm2 of ROM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. WAS ZERO, DELIBERATELY, AND ZERO IS NOT PHYSICAL. The reason zero was defensible is now gone: the previous note held it at zero because the submitted companion of 0.006 W/mm2 had no derivation, and "a companion nobody derived is not evidence". A derivation now exists and it is built entirely on this file's own entries, so it can be checked line by line: the verified SRAM companion 0.005 W/mm2 over 24.07e6 usable bits/mm2 at 0.8 V is 0.260 nA per 6T cell; over 4 off devices in a 6T that is 0.065 nA per device; a NOR mask-ROM cell has ONE off device, so at this file's own ROM capacity density of 129.63e6 bits/mm2 (0.027 um2 6T cell x 0.33 ratio / 0.52 array efficiency) the array leaks 0.065 nA x 129.63e6 x 0.8 V = 6.73e-3 W/mm2. It rests on five `assumed` entries and is graded accordingly. THE DERIVATION DECLINES TWO REAL ROM-FAVOURABLE CREDITS, which is why it is safe at the point: an array with no read-stability constraint may use HVT or long-channel devices for free, and roughly half of a via-programmed NOR array's cells have no bitline leakage path at all. Qualitative corroboration that ROM array leakage is not negligible: TOM's entire third contribution is power-gating inactive ROM banks, 25.813 W down to 5.33 W. DIRECTION AND WHERE IT BINDS: this is a straight charge against the ROM side and it favours the GPU. On the current HC1 reconstruction the 432.4 mm2 ROM array contributes 2.90 W: it moves the static result from the 50.0 W clocked-idle floor to a 52.54 W enumeration and the whole gate from 85.0 W to 87.6 W -- and it matters on the wafer-class designs, where a 50 W per-device floor cannot bind and 6.7e-3 W/mm2 over hundreds of thousands of mm2 is thousands of watts. Sweep 1.3e-3 to 2.6e-2; note that `range_high` moves DOWN 13% from the incumbent 0.03, because the band is now a bracket around a derived point rather than the ceiling of an undocumented reconstruction, and that 13% is the only part of this edit that runs in the ROM side's favour.
static_leakage_w_per_mm2_rom_array.source: derived on this file's own entries: power.static_leakage_w_per_mm2.sram_array, sram.array_efficiency, nodes.N7.sram_hd_bitcell_um2, rom.cell_to_sram_cell_area_ratio and rom.array_efficiency, with one off device per NOR mask-ROM cell against four in a 6T ; qualitative corroboration from Guan et al., TOM, arXiv:2602.20662 (bank power gating 25.813 W -> 5.33 W)

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_sram_array.note: 0.005 W per mm2 of SRAM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. This companion's chain VERIFIED and is carried at the verifier's value, one third below the 0.015 that the same submission's 'of array' companion implied. 0.65 array efficiency over a 0.027 um2 N7 6T bitcell is 24.07 Mbit/mm2 of usable cells; at 0.05-1.0 nA of off current per cell and 0.8 V that is 0.96-19.3 mW/mm2, and the point sits at the geometric-centre end of it. Cross-check that reproduces: 537 Mbit at that density is 22.3 mm2 and 0.021-0.43 W. Charged over SRAM array area only -- the KV store on a ROM part, and the non-logic share of a published GPU die.
static_leakage_w_per_mm2_sram_array.source: TSMC N7 0.027 um2 6T HD bitcell (this file, nodes.N7) at sram.array_efficiency, times a per-cell off current of 0.05-1.0 nA at 0.8 V; no vendor SRAM macro leakage published for the target arrays

clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle.note: 8.5e-11 J per mm2 per clock cycle for the clock network -- the distribution tree, its buffers and the clock pins it drives -- charged on every clocked mm2 whether or not a byte moves. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 15% DOWN from the submitted 1.0e-10, which violated its own stated selection rule ('take the estimator that closes less of the gap' yields 8.48e-11 and the submission rounded up past it). WHAT THIS NUMBER ACTUALLY IS, and the note must say it plainly: clock distribution taken as 20-45% of a shipping NON-ANCHOR GPU's published TDP density, applied at that part's published clock. P100 is 300 W over 610 mm2 at 1480 MHz = 0.492 W/mm2 = 3.32e-10 J/mm2/cycle; GV100 is 300 W over 815 mm2 at 1530 MHz = 0.368 W/mm2 = 2.41e-10; 30% of each, geometric mean, is 8.5e-11. No node correction from 16FF+/12FFN to N7/N6 and no modern-clock-gating discount is applied, and the 20-45% band itself comes from 1992-2004 CPUs (Alpha 21064/21164, MCORE, XScale) with little fine-grain gating. THE SUBMITTED BOTTOM-UP ROUTE IS NOT A SECOND ESTIMATOR AND MUST NOT BE SOLD AS ONE: rebuilt on measured 7 nm primitives instead of its invented capacitance scaling (ASAP7 DFFHQNx1 measures 1.095 fJ/cycle against the Nangate45 DFF_X1's 3.626, a ratio of 0.302 where the submission assumed 0.116) and on this repository's own post-route SPEF-extracted clock tree (4.329 mW of clock group against 0.987 mW of raw CK pin load, a 4.39x distribution multiplier where the submission asserted 1.925x), it returns 578 W on an A100 rated at 400 W. It is reported as a CEILING CHECK THAT FAILS. What the A100's TDP actually bounds is the product of flip-flop areal density and enabled fraction, to about 63k/mm2 against the 435k x 0.59 = 257k the bottom-up assumed; that 4x is the honest statement of what is unknown here. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a published or measured clock-network power fraction for a post-2015 clock-gated GPU or accelerator (AccelWattch/GPUWattch-class validated breakdown, or a vendor statement). Range 3e-11 to 1.6e-10 spans ~12% (an aggressively gated part at a memory-bound decode step, XScale's 17% being the cited low outlier) to 45%, the top of the published band.
clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle.source: NVIDIA Ampere architecture whitepaper, die area / TDP / clock table for P100 (610 mm2, 300 W, 1480 MHz, 16FF+) and GV100 (815 mm2, 300 W, 1530 MHz, 12FFN), verified verbatim ; the 20-45% clock-network power fraction band from Dobberpuhl 1992, Restle 2001 and Donno 2004, which could not be re-fetched and is the single load-bearing input

clock_frequency_hz.note: 1.0 GHz for a modelled design that has no published clock. WHAT THIS KEY FEEDS, STATED EXHAUSTIVELY, BECAUSE IT HAS BEEN MISREAD AS THE COMPUTE ROOF AND IT IS NOT: it is read in exactly one place, `Technology.clock_frequency_hz`, and consumed in exactly one, the clock leg of `device_static_power` -- clock watts per mm2 = `clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle` x this. IT SETS NO RATE. The compute roof on both sides comes from `compute.format_roofs_ops_s` divided by the anchor die area and scaled by `nodes.*.logic_density_vs_n7`, and it does not read this key; a published part uses its own `clock_frequency_hz` here and ignores this key entirely. So this constant reaches a rate ONLY through power -> thermal_scale, and only at points where thermal binds. WHERE IT IS NEVERTHELESS LOAD-BEARING FOR LATENCY, WHICH IS THE PART NOTHING ENFORCED: `latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s` and `latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s` are both DERIVED IN FABRIC CYCLES against this key and both bands are exact integer cycle counts at 1 GHz -- fill/drain 16 / 32 / 128 cycles, sequencer 1 / 3 / 8 cycles -- while neither entry reads it. Moving this key without moving those two silently breaks their stated derivations, and those two ARE on the critical path of every token on both sides. `tools/run_roofline_studies.py` now REFUSES that inconsistency: the consistency audit recomputes both entries' cycle counts at this frequency and fails if either point or either band end stops being the cycle count its own note claims. THE ASAP7 EVIDENCE WAS CHECKED AGAINST THIS CONSTANT AND DOES NOT RETIRE IT. This repository holds three routed, timing-PASSING ASAP7 blocks: `results/physical_abi3/asap7/reduction_s8_g2/pnr.json` at a 2.25 ns period (fmax about 455 MHz), `.../add_bf16_sram_engine/pnr.json` at 4.4 ns (about 239 MHz) and `.../matmul_bf16_sram_engine/pnr.json` at 18.0 ns (57.959 MHz). None closes at 1 GHz. FIVE REASONS THEY DO NOT RETIRE THIS KEY, IN DESCENDING ORDER OF FORCE. (1) They are not evidence about this quantity at all: this key sets clock ENERGY, and those are fmax figures for three specific blocks. (2) THE 18 ns PERIOD IS NOT A FABRIC CLOCK. `rtl/ot_ta_matmul_bf16_sram_engine.sv` is a serial reference executor: one 16-bit SRAM read per request/wait pair, and a combinational `fp32_mul_rne` feeding `fp32_add_rne` inside ONE cycle, unpipelined and unretimed. That cycle does ONE multiply-accumulate at most, and the state machine spends two cycles per MAC, so the hypothesis that the block does N MACs per cycle and that 58 MHz x N is consistent with 1 GHz is FALSE IN THE OTHER DIRECTION -- the block is slower than one MAC per cycle, not faster. What 18 ns measures is an unpipelined FP32 fused multiply-add plus a nonfinite check, which is a property of RTL written for arithmetic clarity rather than for frequency. (3) THE RULE. `docs/METHODOLOGY.md` SS 9 and the W9 claim boundary in `docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md` both state that no frequency, area or energy from a 130 nm OR PREDICTIVE-7 nm open PDK may be scaled to N6/N5/N7/N4. That is not the SKY130 prohibition in W8.3 being silently extended: it is a separate rule that names predictive-7 nm explicitly, and this repository's own ASAP7 artifact declares its evidence class as "predictive open-PDK ... not a foundry PDK, not TSMC N7/N6/N5, not silicon". (4) THE 18 ns IS THE ARITHMETIC PACKAGE, AND THIS REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY MEASURED THAT SEPARATELY AND ATTRIBUTED IT TO A CODING SHAPE. OI-44 in `docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md` synthesised each operation alone as one combinational cloud between registers: on SKY130 HD `ot_fp32_rne_pkg::fp32_add_rne` needs a 66.97 ns period (`results/physical_abi3/sky130hd/a3_numeric_probes/fp32_add.json`) and `fp32_mul_rne` needs 29.385 ns (`.../fp32_mul.json`), and the cause is recorded there as a 27-iteration cancellation-normalisation loop -- "a coding shape rather than a technology limit". The matmul engine's one cycle chains exactly those two functions, so the ASAP7 period is that package's delay and not a fabric's. Two further facts from the routed artifact itself put the same point beyond argument: `place_and_route.metrics.macro_count` is 0 and `sequential_cell_count` is 8,879, so the 256-entry input buffer and the 64-entry accumulator and auxiliary buffers are synthesised as flip-flop arrays, and every operand in that critical path is read through a combinational 256:1 and 64:1 register-file mux before it reaches the multiplier. No shipping fabric clocks a datapath shaped like that, and the block was never written to be one -- its header says it exists for bounded data-bearing execution and exact arithmetic. (5) ASAP7 IS PESSIMISTIC AND THE DIRECTION IS KNOWN: it is a predictive academic library with no foundry characterisation, no custom datapath cells, no SRAM compiler and conservative wire models, and the three blocks above were synthesised by an open flow from RTL with no pipelining, no retiming and no floorplanning. A predictive-PDK number is not silicon and none of the five reasons above is an argument that 1 GHz is RIGHT -- only that this evidence cannot set it. THE VALUE AND THE BAND ARE THEREFORE UNCHANGED at 1.0 GHz swept 0.5-2.0 GHz, AND THE BAND IS NOT WIDENED DOWNWARD ON THIS EVIDENCE. Note the direction that widening would run: no rate depends on this key, so lowering it buys clock power for free and RAISES the ROM side's thermal headroom, while the GPU comparators' clocks are published and do not move. A band widened to the ASAP7 fmax would be a one-sided credit to the ROM side bought with a number the methodology forbids using. THE SENSITIVITY IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED: `results/roofline/*/analytical.json -> fabric_clock_sensitivity` re-runs the study at both band ends and at the ASAP7 figures, with the two cycle-derived latency constants moved consistently, and reports what each does to every headline. WHAT THIS KEY IS WORTH ON THE HC1 POWER GATE, and the HC1 clock negative is registered HERE because Taalas publishes none: 0.5 GHz gives 70.16 W, 1.0 GHz gives 70.16 W (the 50 W clocked-idle floor binds below about 1 GHz, so the term is INERT there) and 2.0 GHz gives 75.81 W, moving the gate from 0.2807x to 0.3032x. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a published clock for any mask-ROM or compute-in-ROM inference die, or a foundry-PDK implementation of this program's own datapath at a target node.
clock_frequency_hz.source: no clock published for any mask-ROM or compute-in-ROM inference die; Taalas publishes no microarchitecture and no frequency (taalas.com, The Next Platform "Clock speed information is not disclosed", The Register, ServeTheHome, CNX, Wavect, Kaitchup, 13 Taalas patents with zero GHz/MHz hits, Hot Chips 2026 program, ISSCC 2026 advance program) ; checked against and NOT retired by this repository's routed ASAP7 blocks at results/physical_abi3/asap7/, which docs/METHODOLOGY.md SS 9 and the W9 claim boundary in docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md ("no frequency, area or energy from a 130 nm or predictive-7 nm open PDK may be scaled to N6/N5/N7/N4") forbid scaling to a target node ; the 18 ns period is attributed to the arithmetic package by this repository's own SKY130 HD per-operation measurements at results/physical_abi3/sky130hd/a3_numeric_probes/

clock_region_multiplier_logic.note: 1.0 by definition: clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle is calibrated on a GPU's whole-die TDP density, and a GPU die is the reference clocked-logic region. Compute, interconnect, HBM PHY and overhead area all carry this multiplier. HBM and SerDes PHY is explicitly NOT set to zero: the argument that its energy is already inside energy.hbm_j_per_byte is wrong, because that term is a per-byte access energy and carries no idle PHY or controller floor.
clock_region_multiplier_logic.source: definition of the calibration region for the clock term

clock_region_multiplier_rom_array.note: 0.15 -- a mask-ROM array's clocked leaf count per mm2 against a logic region's. VERIFIER'S CAUTION CARRIED, AND IT IS THE REASON THE RANGE REACHES 0.5: 0.15 was derived from a LEAF COUNT, but the measured post-route decomposition in this repository shows distribution -- largely wire, whose length is set by AREA and not by leaf count -- at ~3.4x the leaf pin load. Array-region clock power should therefore scale SUB-LINEARLY with leaf density, so 0.15 is likely optimistic for the ROM side and its low end needs a wire argument rather than a latch count. This multiplier and power.fabric_clock_hz multiply, and together they set the W/mm2 asymmetry between the two sides of the comparison this study exists to make, so they are swept jointly and never asserted.
clock_region_multiplier_rom_array.source: no published clock-network power for a mask-ROM or compute-in-ROM array; leaf-count argument against the measured wire-dominated distribution at rtl/build/implementation_campaign (post-route, SPEF-extracted)

clock_region_multiplier_sram_array.note: 0.15, the same class as a ROM array and for the same reason: an SRAM macro's clocked elements are its periphery -- decoders, sense-amp timing, output latches -- and not a flip-flop field over the bitcell area. Swept 0.05-0.5 jointly with the ROM multiplier and the fabric clock.
clock_region_multiplier_sram_array.source: no vendor SRAM macro clock-power breakdown published

clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device.note: 50 W per device of traffic-independent power, applied as a FLOOR on the enumerated static terms and not as an addend -- static power is max(leakage + clock + memory-interface idle, this) -- because leakage and clock ARE most of the physics inside a measured clocked-idle reading and adding both would double-count it. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, from 52 W and, more importantly, on SCOPE: the submission named this gpu_device_fixed_overhead_w and charged it to GPU-class devices only, which is the same class of error as a fitted multiplier and harder to see -- the evidence assembled for it says the floor is clock distribution plus memory-interface clocking on a large clocked die, and a compute-in-ROM part at 815 mm2 with a clocked ROM array and SRAM KV has both. It is charged to BOTH sides here. The value is the mean of four parts' clocked-idle fraction of TDP applied to 400 W: H100 SXM 72.5 W of 700 W = 10.357% (measured, NREL-class facility study); A100 SXM ~50 W of 400 W = 12.5%; B200 140 W of 1000 W = 14.0%; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 77.03 W of 600 W = 12.84%, which is EXECUTED HERE and is the artifact named above. The submission's 84.6 W reading was REFUTED as an instrumentation artifact -- it averaged a window 4-10 s after a 411 W load stopped, which straddles the decay tail (t+0 s = 116.72 W, t+5 s = 76.95 W in the committed trace) -- and the replicated steady clocked-idle state is 77.03 W across 22 samples at 2610 MHz SM / 13365 MHz memory, util 0. Note what 'clocked' means: the same board at a genuinely idle P-state drops to 7.8 W median, so this is the floor for a device that is up and serving, not a power-gated one. Two caveats the submission hid: the two 'methods' were one, because the low-bandwidth sweep points were produced by duty-cycling and so return clocked-idle power by construction; and the P8 decomposition drops the memory clock 33x at the same time as the SM clock, so roughly 30 W of the 69 W delta is the memory subsystem, which is why memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack is a separate term. The published cross-check is independent and close: SC'25 Table 2 measures P_const = 54 W for the A100 (72 W GH200, 88 W MI250X GCD, 69 W MI300A). The 100 W upper end the submission proposed was REJECTED -- the A100's 100 W Min Power Limit is the lowest cap the driver will enforce, a policy floor and not a consumption measurement. The defensible top is the clocked-and-issuing figure, 80 W.
clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device.source: Executed on this machine: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, 600 W, 1,141 nvidia-smi samples, artifact committed at results/roofline/gpu_clocked_idle_floor.json. Published legs: Vercellino et al., Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning, arXiv:2604.07345 (2026), Appendix A, 'each idle GPU spent 72.5 W on average' on 700 W H100 SXM ; Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 2 P_const = 54 W for the A100, as the independent cross-check

memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack.note: 2.8 W per HBM stack of traffic-independent DRAM device, PHY and controller power -- standby, refresh and an up-and-trained interface -- charged whether or not a byte moves. The submitted companion to the HBM energy term was filed as `measured` at 3.7 W/stack with a range of 3.27-4.27 and BOTH WERE REFUTED. The grade could not stand: its only source is an anonymous artifact-evaluation drop for a paper still under review -- no authors, no venue, no DOI -- and this file's own vocabulary reserves `measured` for fabricated silicon in a peer-reviewed venue. The range was false precision: both endpoints were the same 6.40 W measurement times two similar ratios, so they could not disagree. The honest interval is 1.2 W (DRAM device standby plus refresh, capacity-scaled from real HBM2 stack IDD2/IDD3N1 measurements of 272/246 mA at 1.2 V after subtracting a per-chip no-HBM baseline) to 6.40 W (a measured H200 memory-rail idle per stack, if HBM2e's subsystem idle is no lower than HBM3e's) -- a 5x band whose geometric centre is 2.8. This term is why clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device is a floor and not an addend: on the A100 the two describe overlapping physics, and SC'25's published P_const of 54 W is the whole traffic-independent draw that both are estimating. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: an Ampere-generation memory-rail measurement (Ampere does not expose the field), a vendor HBM2e stack IDD specification, or A100 baseboard rail telemetry.
memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack.source: HBM2 stack IDD2/IDD3N1/IDD5B measurements and an H200 memory-rail idle reading, both from the CMU-SAFARI/HBM-Power artifact drop (2026) for a paper under review -- no venue, no DOI, so this cannot be graded above `assumed` ; cross-checked against Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 2

rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

sram_capacity_density_bits_mm2.note: 1e6 um2/mm2 / (bitcell_um2 / array_efficiency). N5 6T high-density SRAM array capacity density in bits/mm2
sram_capacity_density_bits_mm2.source: https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/283487-tsmcs-5nm-0-021um2-sram-cell-using-euv-and-high-mobility-channel-with-write-assist-at-isscc2020/ ; no vendor macro floorplan published for the target arrays

sram_read_bandwidth_density_bytes_s_mm2.note: (anchor_sram_read_bytes_s / anchor_die_area_mm2) * (anchor_bitcell_um2 / target_bitcell_um2). N5 SRAM array read-bandwidth density in bytes/s/mm2; the anchor rate is charged against WHOLE-die area and then applied only to array area, which is conservative

sram_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: fraction of the SRAM array's peak read rate sustained by a real gather pattern

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_logic.note: 0.06 W per mm2 of STANDARD-CELL (logic) region at a 7 nm-class node, at 0.70-0.75 V and 85-105 C junction, on a mix weighted toward RVT. THE UNIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS THE SUBMISSION'S worst defect: it is per mm2 of standard-cell region, NOT per mm2 of die, so on a part that is mostly array this term is charged over the logic only. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 2x UP from the submitted 0.03. The chain is: an executed ASAP7 place-and-route base of 0.74e-3 W/mm2 of 100%-filled cell area at 25 C/0.70 V typical (from this repository's own results/physical_abi3/asap7 metadata, cross-checked three ways against the liberty's 1 pW leakage unit and against real-scale ASAP7 cell areas), times a threshold-flavour mix, a temperature factor and a voltage factor. The correction is in the threshold ladder: the submission put RELATIVE per-flavour offsets (SLVT 0, LVT 0.071, RVT 0.142 V) inside an exponential that needs the ABSOLUTE saturation threshold, and a device with Vth = 0 is not off. That ladder predicts a 25->100 C ratio of 12.69x at typical/nominal, which is BELOW the 13.82x ASAP7's own SS liberty measures at a slower process AND a lower voltage -- impossible. Re-anchoring to absolute Vth_sat (RVT 0.24, LVT 0.169, SLVT 0.098 V, the lowest ladder clearing that floor) moves the combined mix x T x V factor from 14.8 to 25.3 at the low end and 62.4 to 114.8 at the point. The submission's structural claim that leakier flavours scale less steeply, so mix and temperature partly cancel, is separately FALSIFIED by the same library: measured INVx1 FF/TT ratios are 0.638 / 0.546 / 0.646 across RVT/LVT/SLVT -- flat and non-monotonic -- where the model needs a 1.5x spread. The high end 0.20 is CAPPED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE CHAIN: the chain's own 40/40/20 mix at 105 C and 0.85 V gives 0.43 W/mm2, which is 86% of thermal.cooling_limit_w_per_mm2 and is not physical for a shipping part; 0.19-0.20 is where an A100 lands at ~39% of TDP, the top of ReGate's measured 30-72% static-power band. Grade stays `assumed` and correctly so: ASAP7 is a predictive academic PDK, no datacentre die's Vt mix is published anywhere, and the absolute threshold ladder is inferred from Ioff-per-micron rather than read off a datasheet. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a foundry N7/N6 leakage-per-mm2 figure at a stated PVT, or an ASAP7 SRAM-flavour and LVT/SLVT SS liberty.
static_leakage_w_per_mm2_logic.source: ASAP7 7.5-track predictive PDK NLDM libraries (RVT/LVT/SLVT TT and SS corners) and this repository's executed ASAP7 place-and-route leakage at results/physical_abi3/asap7/add_bf16_sram_engine/pnr_artifacts/metadata.json ; ReGate, MICRO 2025, arXiv:2508.02536, which reports static power at 30-72% of NPU energy

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_rom_array.note: 6.7e-3 W per mm2 of ROM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. WAS ZERO, DELIBERATELY, AND ZERO IS NOT PHYSICAL. The reason zero was defensible is now gone: the previous note held it at zero because the submitted companion of 0.006 W/mm2 had no derivation, and "a companion nobody derived is not evidence". A derivation now exists and it is built entirely on this file's own entries, so it can be checked line by line: the verified SRAM companion 0.005 W/mm2 over 24.07e6 usable bits/mm2 at 0.8 V is 0.260 nA per 6T cell; over 4 off devices in a 6T that is 0.065 nA per device; a NOR mask-ROM cell has ONE off device, so at this file's own ROM capacity density of 129.63e6 bits/mm2 (0.027 um2 6T cell x 0.33 ratio / 0.52 array efficiency) the array leaks 0.065 nA x 129.63e6 x 0.8 V = 6.73e-3 W/mm2. It rests on five `assumed` entries and is graded accordingly. THE DERIVATION DECLINES TWO REAL ROM-FAVOURABLE CREDITS, which is why it is safe at the point: an array with no read-stability constraint may use HVT or long-channel devices for free, and roughly half of a via-programmed NOR array's cells have no bitline leakage path at all. Qualitative corroboration that ROM array leakage is not negligible: TOM's entire third contribution is power-gating inactive ROM banks, 25.813 W down to 5.33 W. DIRECTION AND WHERE IT BINDS: this is a straight charge against the ROM side and it favours the GPU. On the current HC1 reconstruction the 432.4 mm2 ROM array contributes 2.90 W: it moves the static result from the 50.0 W clocked-idle floor to a 52.54 W enumeration and the whole gate from 85.0 W to 87.6 W -- and it matters on the wafer-class designs, where a 50 W per-device floor cannot bind and 6.7e-3 W/mm2 over hundreds of thousands of mm2 is thousands of watts. Sweep 1.3e-3 to 2.6e-2; note that `range_high` moves DOWN 13% from the incumbent 0.03, because the band is now a bracket around a derived point rather than the ceiling of an undocumented reconstruction, and that 13% is the only part of this edit that runs in the ROM side's favour.
static_leakage_w_per_mm2_rom_array.source: derived on this file's own entries: power.static_leakage_w_per_mm2.sram_array, sram.array_efficiency, nodes.N7.sram_hd_bitcell_um2, rom.cell_to_sram_cell_area_ratio and rom.array_efficiency, with one off device per NOR mask-ROM cell against four in a 6T ; qualitative corroboration from Guan et al., TOM, arXiv:2602.20662 (bank power gating 25.813 W -> 5.33 W)

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_sram_array.note: 0.005 W per mm2 of SRAM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. This companion's chain VERIFIED and is carried at the verifier's value, one third below the 0.015 that the same submission's 'of array' companion implied. 0.65 array efficiency over a 0.027 um2 N7 6T bitcell is 24.07 Mbit/mm2 of usable cells; at 0.05-1.0 nA of off current per cell and 0.8 V that is 0.96-19.3 mW/mm2, and the point sits at the geometric-centre end of it. Cross-check that reproduces: 537 Mbit at that density is 22.3 mm2 and 0.021-0.43 W. Charged over SRAM array area only -- the KV store on a ROM part, and the non-logic share of a published GPU die.
static_leakage_w_per_mm2_sram_array.source: TSMC N7 0.027 um2 6T HD bitcell (this file, nodes.N7) at sram.array_efficiency, times a per-cell off current of 0.05-1.0 nA at 0.8 V; no vendor SRAM macro leakage published for the target arrays

clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle.note: 8.5e-11 J per mm2 per clock cycle for the clock network -- the distribution tree, its buffers and the clock pins it drives -- charged on every clocked mm2 whether or not a byte moves. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 15% DOWN from the submitted 1.0e-10, which violated its own stated selection rule ('take the estimator that closes less of the gap' yields 8.48e-11 and the submission rounded up past it). WHAT THIS NUMBER ACTUALLY IS, and the note must say it plainly: clock distribution taken as 20-45% of a shipping NON-ANCHOR GPU's published TDP density, applied at that part's published clock. P100 is 300 W over 610 mm2 at 1480 MHz = 0.492 W/mm2 = 3.32e-10 J/mm2/cycle; GV100 is 300 W over 815 mm2 at 1530 MHz = 0.368 W/mm2 = 2.41e-10; 30% of each, geometric mean, is 8.5e-11. No node correction from 16FF+/12FFN to N7/N6 and no modern-clock-gating discount is applied, and the 20-45% band itself comes from 1992-2004 CPUs (Alpha 21064/21164, MCORE, XScale) with little fine-grain gating. THE SUBMITTED BOTTOM-UP ROUTE IS NOT A SECOND ESTIMATOR AND MUST NOT BE SOLD AS ONE: rebuilt on measured 7 nm primitives instead of its invented capacitance scaling (ASAP7 DFFHQNx1 measures 1.095 fJ/cycle against the Nangate45 DFF_X1's 3.626, a ratio of 0.302 where the submission assumed 0.116) and on this repository's own post-route SPEF-extracted clock tree (4.329 mW of clock group against 0.987 mW of raw CK pin load, a 4.39x distribution multiplier where the submission asserted 1.925x), it returns 578 W on an A100 rated at 400 W. It is reported as a CEILING CHECK THAT FAILS. What the A100's TDP actually bounds is the product of flip-flop areal density and enabled fraction, to about 63k/mm2 against the 435k x 0.59 = 257k the bottom-up assumed; that 4x is the honest statement of what is unknown here. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a published or measured clock-network power fraction for a post-2015 clock-gated GPU or accelerator (AccelWattch/GPUWattch-class validated breakdown, or a vendor statement). Range 3e-11 to 1.6e-10 spans ~12% (an aggressively gated part at a memory-bound decode step, XScale's 17% being the cited low outlier) to 45%, the top of the published band.
clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle.source: NVIDIA Ampere architecture whitepaper, die area / TDP / clock table for P100 (610 mm2, 300 W, 1480 MHz, 16FF+) and GV100 (815 mm2, 300 W, 1530 MHz, 12FFN), verified verbatim ; the 20-45% clock-network power fraction band from Dobberpuhl 1992, Restle 2001 and Donno 2004, which could not be re-fetched and is the single load-bearing input

clock_frequency_hz.note: 1.0 GHz for a modelled design that has no published clock. WHAT THIS KEY FEEDS, STATED EXHAUSTIVELY, BECAUSE IT HAS BEEN MISREAD AS THE COMPUTE ROOF AND IT IS NOT: it is read in exactly one place, `Technology.clock_frequency_hz`, and consumed in exactly one, the clock leg of `device_static_power` -- clock watts per mm2 = `clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle` x this. IT SETS NO RATE. The compute roof on both sides comes from `compute.format_roofs_ops_s` divided by the anchor die area and scaled by `nodes.*.logic_density_vs_n7`, and it does not read this key; a published part uses its own `clock_frequency_hz` here and ignores this key entirely. So this constant reaches a rate ONLY through power -> thermal_scale, and only at points where thermal binds. WHERE IT IS NEVERTHELESS LOAD-BEARING FOR LATENCY, WHICH IS THE PART NOTHING ENFORCED: `latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s` and `latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s` are both DERIVED IN FABRIC CYCLES against this key and both bands are exact integer cycle counts at 1 GHz -- fill/drain 16 / 32 / 128 cycles, sequencer 1 / 3 / 8 cycles -- while neither entry reads it. Moving this key without moving those two silently breaks their stated derivations, and those two ARE on the critical path of every token on both sides. `tools/run_roofline_studies.py` now REFUSES that inconsistency: the consistency audit recomputes both entries' cycle counts at this frequency and fails if either point or either band end stops being the cycle count its own note claims. THE ASAP7 EVIDENCE WAS CHECKED AGAINST THIS CONSTANT AND DOES NOT RETIRE IT. This repository holds three routed, timing-PASSING ASAP7 blocks: `results/physical_abi3/asap7/reduction_s8_g2/pnr.json` at a 2.25 ns period (fmax about 455 MHz), `.../add_bf16_sram_engine/pnr.json` at 4.4 ns (about 239 MHz) and `.../matmul_bf16_sram_engine/pnr.json` at 18.0 ns (57.959 MHz). None closes at 1 GHz. FIVE REASONS THEY DO NOT RETIRE THIS KEY, IN DESCENDING ORDER OF FORCE. (1) They are not evidence about this quantity at all: this key sets clock ENERGY, and those are fmax figures for three specific blocks. (2) THE 18 ns PERIOD IS NOT A FABRIC CLOCK. `rtl/ot_ta_matmul_bf16_sram_engine.sv` is a serial reference executor: one 16-bit SRAM read per request/wait pair, and a combinational `fp32_mul_rne` feeding `fp32_add_rne` inside ONE cycle, unpipelined and unretimed. That cycle does ONE multiply-accumulate at most, and the state machine spends two cycles per MAC, so the hypothesis that the block does N MACs per cycle and that 58 MHz x N is consistent with 1 GHz is FALSE IN THE OTHER DIRECTION -- the block is slower than one MAC per cycle, not faster. What 18 ns measures is an unpipelined FP32 fused multiply-add plus a nonfinite check, which is a property of RTL written for arithmetic clarity rather than for frequency. (3) THE RULE. `docs/METHODOLOGY.md` SS 9 and the W9 claim boundary in `docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md` both state that no frequency, area or energy from a 130 nm OR PREDICTIVE-7 nm open PDK may be scaled to N6/N5/N7/N4. That is not the SKY130 prohibition in W8.3 being silently extended: it is a separate rule that names predictive-7 nm explicitly, and this repository's own ASAP7 artifact declares its evidence class as "predictive open-PDK ... not a foundry PDK, not TSMC N7/N6/N5, not silicon". (4) THE 18 ns IS THE ARITHMETIC PACKAGE, AND THIS REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY MEASURED THAT SEPARATELY AND ATTRIBUTED IT TO A CODING SHAPE. OI-44 in `docs/UNIFIED_EXECUTION_CHECKLIST.md` synthesised each operation alone as one combinational cloud between registers: on SKY130 HD `ot_fp32_rne_pkg::fp32_add_rne` needs a 66.97 ns period (`results/physical_abi3/sky130hd/a3_numeric_probes/fp32_add.json`) and `fp32_mul_rne` needs 29.385 ns (`.../fp32_mul.json`), and the cause is recorded there as a 27-iteration cancellation-normalisation loop -- "a coding shape rather than a technology limit". The matmul engine's one cycle chains exactly those two functions, so the ASAP7 period is that package's delay and not a fabric's. Two further facts from the routed artifact itself put the same point beyond argument: `place_and_route.metrics.macro_count` is 0 and `sequential_cell_count` is 8,879, so the 256-entry input buffer and the 64-entry accumulator and auxiliary buffers are synthesised as flip-flop arrays, and every operand in that critical path is read through a combinational 256:1 and 64:1 register-file mux before it reaches the multiplier. No shipping fabric clocks a datapath shaped like that, and the block was never written to be one -- its header says it exists for bounded data-bearing execution and exact arithmetic. (5) ASAP7 IS PESSIMISTIC AND THE DIRECTION IS KNOWN: it is a predictive academic library with no foundry characterisation, no custom datapath cells, no SRAM compiler and conservative wire models, and the three blocks above were synthesised by an open flow from RTL with no pipelining, no retiming and no floorplanning. A predictive-PDK number is not silicon and none of the five reasons above is an argument that 1 GHz is RIGHT -- only that this evidence cannot set it. THE VALUE AND THE BAND ARE THEREFORE UNCHANGED at 1.0 GHz swept 0.5-2.0 GHz, AND THE BAND IS NOT WIDENED DOWNWARD ON THIS EVIDENCE. Note the direction that widening would run: no rate depends on this key, so lowering it buys clock power for free and RAISES the ROM side's thermal headroom, while the GPU comparators' clocks are published and do not move. A band widened to the ASAP7 fmax would be a one-sided credit to the ROM side bought with a number the methodology forbids using. THE SENSITIVITY IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED: `results/roofline/*/analytical.json -> fabric_clock_sensitivity` re-runs the study at both band ends and at the ASAP7 figures, with the two cycle-derived latency constants moved consistently, and reports what each does to every headline. WHAT THIS KEY IS WORTH ON THE HC1 POWER GATE, and the HC1 clock negative is registered HERE because Taalas publishes none: 0.5 GHz gives 70.16 W, 1.0 GHz gives 70.16 W (the 50 W clocked-idle floor binds below about 1 GHz, so the term is INERT there) and 2.0 GHz gives 75.81 W, moving the gate from 0.2807x to 0.3032x. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a published clock for any mask-ROM or compute-in-ROM inference die, or a foundry-PDK implementation of this program's own datapath at a target node.

clock_region_multiplier_logic.note: 1.0 by definition: clock_energy_j_per_mm2_per_cycle is calibrated on a GPU's whole-die TDP density, and a GPU die is the reference clocked-logic region. Compute, interconnect, HBM PHY and overhead area all carry this multiplier. HBM and SerDes PHY is explicitly NOT set to zero: the argument that its energy is already inside energy.hbm_j_per_byte is wrong, because that term is a per-byte access energy and carries no idle PHY or controller floor.
clock_region_multiplier_logic.source: definition of the calibration region for the clock term

clock_region_multiplier_rom_array.note: 0.15 -- a mask-ROM array's clocked leaf count per mm2 against a logic region's. VERIFIER'S CAUTION CARRIED, AND IT IS THE REASON THE RANGE REACHES 0.5: 0.15 was derived from a LEAF COUNT, but the measured post-route decomposition in this repository shows distribution -- largely wire, whose length is set by AREA and not by leaf count -- at ~3.4x the leaf pin load. Array-region clock power should therefore scale SUB-LINEARLY with leaf density, so 0.15 is likely optimistic for the ROM side and its low end needs a wire argument rather than a latch count. This multiplier and power.fabric_clock_hz multiply, and together they set the W/mm2 asymmetry between the two sides of the comparison this study exists to make, so they are swept jointly and never asserted.
clock_region_multiplier_rom_array.source: no published clock-network power for a mask-ROM or compute-in-ROM array; leaf-count argument against the measured wire-dominated distribution at rtl/build/implementation_campaign (post-route, SPEF-extracted)

clock_region_multiplier_sram_array.note: 0.15, the same class as a ROM array and for the same reason: an SRAM macro's clocked elements are its periphery -- decoders, sense-amp timing, output latches -- and not a flip-flop field over the bitcell area. Swept 0.05-0.5 jointly with the ROM multiplier and the fabric clock.
clock_region_multiplier_sram_array.source: no vendor SRAM macro clock-power breakdown published

clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device.note: 50 W per device of traffic-independent power, applied as a FLOOR on the enumerated static terms and not as an addend -- static power is max(leakage + clock + memory-interface idle, this) -- because leakage and clock ARE most of the physics inside a measured clocked-idle reading and adding both would double-count it. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, from 52 W and, more importantly, on SCOPE: the submission named this gpu_device_fixed_overhead_w and charged it to GPU-class devices only, which is the same class of error as a fitted multiplier and harder to see -- the evidence assembled for it says the floor is clock distribution plus memory-interface clocking on a large clocked die, and a compute-in-ROM part at 815 mm2 with a clocked ROM array and SRAM KV has both. It is charged to BOTH sides here. The value is the mean of four parts' clocked-idle fraction of TDP applied to 400 W: H100 SXM 72.5 W of 700 W = 10.357% (measured, NREL-class facility study); A100 SXM ~50 W of 400 W = 12.5%; B200 140 W of 1000 W = 14.0%; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 77.03 W of 600 W = 12.84%, which is EXECUTED HERE and is the artifact named above. The submission's 84.6 W reading was REFUTED as an instrumentation artifact -- it averaged a window 4-10 s after a 411 W load stopped, which straddles the decay tail (t+0 s = 116.72 W, t+5 s = 76.95 W in the committed trace) -- and the replicated steady clocked-idle state is 77.03 W across 22 samples at 2610 MHz SM / 13365 MHz memory, util 0. Note what 'clocked' means: the same board at a genuinely idle P-state drops to 7.8 W median, so this is the floor for a device that is up and serving, not a power-gated one. Two caveats the submission hid: the two 'methods' were one, because the low-bandwidth sweep points were produced by duty-cycling and so return clocked-idle power by construction; and the P8 decomposition drops the memory clock 33x at the same time as the SM clock, so roughly 30 W of the 69 W delta is the memory subsystem, which is why memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack is a separate term. The published cross-check is independent and close: SC'25 Table 2 measures P_const = 54 W for the A100 (72 W GH200, 88 W MI250X GCD, 69 W MI300A). The 100 W upper end the submission proposed was REJECTED -- the A100's 100 W Min Power Limit is the lowest cap the driver will enforce, a policy floor and not a consumption measurement. The defensible top is the clocked-and-issuing figure, 80 W.

memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack.note: 2.8 W per HBM stack of traffic-independent DRAM device, PHY and controller power -- standby, refresh and an up-and-trained interface -- charged whether or not a byte moves. The submitted companion to the HBM energy term was filed as `measured` at 3.7 W/stack with a range of 3.27-4.27 and BOTH WERE REFUTED. The grade could not stand: its only source is an anonymous artifact-evaluation drop for a paper still under review -- no authors, no venue, no DOI -- and this file's own vocabulary reserves `measured` for fabricated silicon in a peer-reviewed venue. The range was false precision: both endpoints were the same 6.40 W measurement times two similar ratios, so they could not disagree. The honest interval is 1.2 W (DRAM device standby plus refresh, capacity-scaled from real HBM2 stack IDD2/IDD3N1 measurements of 272/246 mA at 1.2 V after subtracting a per-chip no-HBM baseline) to 6.40 W (a measured H200 memory-rail idle per stack, if HBM2e's subsystem idle is no lower than HBM3e's) -- a 5x band whose geometric centre is 2.8. This term is why clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device is a floor and not an addend: on the A100 the two describe overlapping physics, and SC'25's published P_const of 54 W is the whole traffic-independent draw that both are estimating. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: an Ampere-generation memory-rail measurement (Ampere does not expose the field), a vendor HBM2e stack IDD specification, or A100 baseboard rail telemetry.

rom_read_bandwidth_efficiency.note: Fraction of the ROM array's peak sweep rate sustained in practice. A mask-ROM sweep is the most regular access pattern available -- a compile-time-fixed linear walk of the whole array with no arbitration, no conflicts and no refresh -- so 0.75 is a conservative charge and 0.90-1.00 is arguable. The study reports the underated ceiling alongside it because this derate moves the ROM answer directly.

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_logic.note: 0.06 W per mm2 of STANDARD-CELL (logic) region at a 7 nm-class node, at 0.70-0.75 V and 85-105 C junction, on a mix weighted toward RVT. THE UNIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS THE SUBMISSION'S worst defect: it is per mm2 of standard-cell region, NOT per mm2 of die, so on a part that is mostly array this term is charged over the logic only. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 2x UP from the submitted 0.03. The chain is: an executed ASAP7 place-and-route base of 0.74e-3 W/mm2 of 100%-filled cell area at 25 C/0.70 V typical (from this repository's own results/physical_abi3/asap7 metadata, cross-checked three ways against the liberty's 1 pW leakage unit and against real-scale ASAP7 cell areas), times a threshold-flavour mix, a temperature factor and a voltage factor. The correction is in the threshold ladder: the submission put RELATIVE per-flavour offsets (SLVT 0, LVT 0.071, RVT 0.142 V) inside an exponential that needs the ABSOLUTE saturation threshold, and a device with Vth = 0 is not off. That ladder predicts a 25->100 C ratio of 12.69x at typical/nominal, which is BELOW the 13.82x ASAP7's own SS liberty measures at a slower process AND a lower voltage -- impossible. Re-anchoring to absolute Vth_sat (RVT 0.24, LVT 0.169, SLVT 0.098 V, the lowest ladder clearing that floor) moves the combined mix x T x V factor from 14.8 to 25.3 at the low end and 62.4 to 114.8 at the point. The submission's structural claim that leakier flavours scale less steeply, so mix and temperature partly cancel, is separately FALSIFIED by the same library: measured INVx1 FF/TT ratios are 0.638 / 0.546 / 0.646 across RVT/LVT/SLVT -- flat and non-monotonic -- where the model needs a 1.5x spread. The high end 0.20 is CAPPED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE CHAIN: the chain's own 40/40/20 mix at 105 C and 0.85 V gives 0.43 W/mm2, which is 86% of thermal.cooling_limit_w_per_mm2 and is not physical for a shipping part; 0.19-0.20 is where an A100 lands at ~39% of TDP, the top of ReGate's measured 30-72% static-power band. Grade stays `assumed` and correctly so: ASAP7 is a predictive academic PDK, no datacentre die's Vt mix is published anywhere, and the absolute threshold ladder is inferred from Ioff-per-micron rather than read off a datasheet. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a foundry N7/N6 leakage-per-mm2 figure at a stated PVT, or an ASAP7 SRAM-flavour and LVT/SLVT SS liberty.

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_rom_array.note: 6.7e-3 W per mm2 of ROM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. WAS ZERO, DELIBERATELY, AND ZERO IS NOT PHYSICAL. The reason zero was defensible is now gone: the previous note held it at zero because the submitted companion of 0.006 W/mm2 had no derivation, and "a companion nobody derived is not evidence". A derivation now exists and it is built entirely on this file's own entries, so it can be checked line by line: the verified SRAM companion 0.005 W/mm2 over 24.07e6 usable bits/mm2 at 0.8 V is 0.260 nA per 6T cell; over 4 off devices in a 6T that is 0.065 nA per device; a NOR mask-ROM cell has ONE off device, so at this file's own ROM capacity density of 129.63e6 bits/mm2 (0.027 um2 6T cell x 0.33 ratio / 0.52 array efficiency) the array leaks 0.065 nA x 129.63e6 x 0.8 V = 6.73e-3 W/mm2. It rests on five `assumed` entries and is graded accordingly. THE DERIVATION DECLINES TWO REAL ROM-FAVOURABLE CREDITS, which is why it is safe at the point: an array with no read-stability constraint may use HVT or long-channel devices for free, and roughly half of a via-programmed NOR array's cells have no bitline leakage path at all. Qualitative corroboration that ROM array leakage is not negligible: TOM's entire third contribution is power-gating inactive ROM banks, 25.813 W down to 5.33 W. DIRECTION AND WHERE IT BINDS: this is a straight charge against the ROM side and it favours the GPU. On the current HC1 reconstruction the 432.4 mm2 ROM array contributes 2.90 W: it moves the static result from the 50.0 W clocked-idle floor to a 52.54 W enumeration and the whole gate from 85.0 W to 87.6 W -- and it matters on the wafer-class designs, where a 50 W per-device floor cannot bind and 6.7e-3 W/mm2 over hundreds of thousands of mm2 is thousands of watts. Sweep 1.3e-3 to 2.6e-2; note that `range_high` moves DOWN 13% from the incumbent 0.03, because the band is now a bracket around a derived point rather than the ceiling of an undocumented reconstruction, and that 13% is the only part of this edit that runs in the ROM side's favour.
static_leakage_w_per_mm2_rom_array.source: derived on this file's own entries: power.static_leakage_w_per_mm2.sram_array, sram.array_efficiency, nodes.N7.sram_hd_bitcell_um2, rom.cell_to_sram_cell_area_ratio and rom.array_efficiency, with one off device per NOR mask-ROM cell against four in a 6T ; qualitative corroboration from Guan et al., TOM, arXiv:2602.20662 (bank power gating 25.813 W -> 5.33 W)

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_sram_array.note: 0.005 W per mm2 of SRAM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. This companion's chain VERIFIED and is carried at the verifier's value, one third below the 0.015 that the same submission's 'of array' companion implied. 0.65 array efficiency over a 0.027 um2 N7 6T bitcell is 24.07 Mbit/mm2 of usable cells; at 0.05-1.0 nA of off current per cell and 0.8 V that is 0.96-19.3 mW/mm2, and the point sits at the geometric-centre end of it. clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device.note: 50 W per device of traffic-independent power, applied as a FLOOR on the enumerated static terms and not as an addend -- static power is max(leakage + clock + memory-interface idle, this) -- because leakage and clock ARE most of the physics inside a measured clocked-idle reading and adding both would double-count it. It is charged to BOTH sides here. The value is the mean of four parts' clocked-idle fraction of TDP applied to 400 W: H100 SXM 72.5 W of 700 W = 10.357% (measured, NREL-class facility study); A100 SXM ~50 W of 400 W = 12.5%; B200 140 W of 1000 W = 14.0%; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 77.03 W of 600 W = 12.84%, which is EXECUTED HERE and is the artifact named above. memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack.note: 2.8 W per HBM stack of traffic-independent DRAM device, PHY and controller power -- standby, refresh and an up-and-trained interface -- charged whether or not a byte moves. The grade could not stand: its only source is an anonymous artifact-evaluation drop for a paper still under review -- no authors, no venue, no DOI -- and this file's own vocabulary reserves `measured` for fabricated silicon in a peer-reviewed venue. The range was false precision: both endpoints were the same 6.40 W measurement times two similar ratios, so they could not disagree. The honest interval is 1.2 W (DRAM device standby plus refresh, capacity-scaled from real HBM2 stack IDD2/IDD3N1 measurements of 272/246 mA at 1.2 V after subtracting a per-chip no-HBM baseline) to 6.40 W (a measured H200 memory-rail idle per stack, if HBM2e's subsystem idle is no lower than HBM3e's) -- a 5x band whose geometric centre is 2.8. This term is why clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device is a floor and not an addend: on the A100 the two describe overlapping physics, and SC'25's published P_const of 54 W is the whole traffic-independent draw that both are estimating. static_leakage_w_per_mm2_logic.note: 0.06 W per mm2 of STANDARD-CELL (logic) region at a 7 nm-class node, at 0.70-0.75 V and 85-105 C junction, on a mix weighted toward RVT. THE UNIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS THE SUBMISSION'S worst defect: it is per mm2 of standard-cell region, NOT per mm2 of die, so on a part that is mostly array this term is charged over the logic only. VERIFIER-CORRECTED, 2x UP from the submitted 0.03. The chain is: an executed ASAP7 place-and-route base of 0.74e-3 W/mm2 of 100%-filled cell area at 25 C/0.70 V typical (from this repository's own results/physical_abi3/asap7 metadata, cross-checked three ways against the liberty's 1 pW leakage unit and against real-scale ASAP7 cell areas), times a threshold-flavour mix, a temperature factor and a voltage factor. The correction is in the threshold ladder: the submission put RELATIVE per-flavour offsets (SLVT 0, LVT 0.071, RVT 0.142 V) inside an exponential that needs the ABSOLUTE saturation threshold, and a device with Vth = 0 is not off. That ladder predicts a 25->100 C ratio of 12.69x at typical/nominal, which is BELOW the 13.82x ASAP7's own SS liberty measures at a slower process AND a lower voltage -- impossible. Re-anchoring to absolute Vth_sat (RVT 0.24, LVT 0.169, SLVT 0.098 V, the lowest ladder clearing that floor) moves the combined mix x T x V factor from 14.8 to 25.3 at the low end and 62.4 to 114.8 at the point. The submission's structural claim that leakier flavours scale less steeply, so mix and temperature partly cancel, is separately FALSIFIED by the same library: measured INVx1 FF/TT ratios are 0.638 / 0.546 / 0.646 across RVT/LVT/SLVT -- flat and non-monotonic -- where the model needs a 1.5x spread. The high end 0.20 is CAPPED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE CHAIN: the chain's own 40/40/20 mix at 105 C and 0.85 V gives 0.43 W/mm2, which is 86% of thermal.cooling_limit_w_per_mm2 and is not physical for a shipping part; 0.19-0.20 is where an A100 lands at ~39% of TDP, the top of ReGate's measured 30-72% static-power band. Grade stays `assumed` and correctly so: ASAP7 is a predictive academic PDK, no datacentre die's Vt mix is published anywhere, and the absolute threshold ladder is inferred from Ioff-per-micron rather than read off a datasheet. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a foundry N7/N6 leakage-per-mm2 figure at a stated PVT, or an ASAP7 SRAM-flavour and LVT/SLVT SS liberty.

static_leakage_w_per_mm2_rom_array.note: 6.7e-3 W per mm2 of ROM ARRAY at a 7 nm-class node. WAS ZERO, DELIBERATELY, AND ZERO IS NOT PHYSICAL. The reason zero was defensible is now gone: the previous note held it at zero because the submitted companion of 0.006 W/mm2 had no derivation, and "a companion nobody derived is not evidence". A derivation now exists and it is built entirely on this file's own entries, so it can be checked line by line: the verified SRAM companion 0.005 W/mm2 over 24.07e6 usable bits/mm2 at 0.8 V is 0.260 nA per 6T cell; over 4 off devices in a 6T that is 0.065 nA per device; a NOR mask-ROM cell has ONE off device, so at this file's own ROM capacity density of 129.63e6 bits/mm2 (0.027 um2 6T cell x 0.33 ratio / 0.52 array efficiency) the array leaks 0.065 nA x 129.63e6 x 0.8 V = 6.73e-3 W/mm2. It rests on five `assumed` entries and is graded accordingly. THE DERIVATION DECLINES TWO REAL ROM-FAVOURABLE CREDITS, which is why it is safe at the point: an array with no read-stability constraint may use HVT or long-channel devices for free, and roughly half of a via-programmed NOR array's cells have no bitline leakage path at all. Qualitative corroboration that ROM array leakage is not negligible: TOM's entire third contribution is power-gating inactive ROM banks, 25.813 W down to 5.33 W. DIRECTION AND WHERE IT BINDS: this is a straight charge against the ROM side and it favours the GPU. On the current HC1 reconstruction the 432.4 mm2 ROM array contributes 2.90 W: it moves the static result from the 50.0 W clocked-idle floor to a 52.54 W enumeration and the whole gate from 85.0 W to 87.6 W -- and it matters on the wafer-class designs, where a 50 W per-device floor cannot bind and 6.7e-3 W/mm2 over hundreds of thousands of mm2 is thousands of watts. Sweep 1.3e-3 to 2.6e-2; note that `range_high` moves DOWN 13% from the incumbent 0.03, because the band is now a bracket around a derived point rather than the ceiling of an undocumented reconstruction, and that 13% is the only part of this edit that runs in the ROM side's favour.

VERIFIER-CORRECTED, from 52 W and, more importantly, on SCOPE: the submission named this gpu_device_fixed_overhead_w and charged it to GPU-class devices only, which is the same class of error as a fitted multiplier and harder to see -- the evidence assembled for it says the floor is clock distribution plus memory-interface clocking on a large clocked die, and a compute-in-ROM part at 815 mm2 with a clocked ROM array and SRAM KV has both. It is charged to BOTH sides here. The value is the mean of four parts' clocked-idle fraction of TDP applied to 400 W: H100 SXM 72.5 W of 700 W = 10.357% (measured, NREL-class facility study); A100 SXM ~50 W of 400 W = 12.5%; B200 140 W of 1000 W = 14.0%; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 77.03 W of 600 W = 12.84%, which is EXECUTED HERE and is the artifact named above. The submission's 84.6 W reading was REFUTED as an instrumentation artifact -- it averaged a window 4-10 s after a 411 W load stopped, which straddles the decay tail (t+0 s = 116.72 W, t+5 s = 76.95 W in the committed trace) -- and the replicated steady clocked-idle state is 77.03 W across 22 samples at 2610 MHz SM / 13365 MHz memory, util 0. Note what 'clocked' means: the same board at a genuinely idle P-state drops to 7.8 W median, so this is the floor for a device that is up and serving, not a power-gated one. Two caveats the submission hid: the two 'methods' were one, because the low-bandwidth sweep points were produced by duty-cycling and so return clocked-idle power by construction; and the P8 decomposition drops the memory clock 33x at the same time as the SM clock, so roughly 30 W of the 69 W delta is the memory subsystem, which is why memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack is a separate term. The published cross-check is independent and close: SC'25 Table 2 measures P_const = 54 W for the A100 (72 W GH200, 88 W MI250X GCD, 69 W MI300A). The 100 W upper end the submission proposed was REJECTED -- the A100's 100 W Min Power Limit is the lowest cap the driver will enforce, a policy floor and not a consumption measurement. The defensible top is the clocked-and-issuing figure, 80 W.
clocked_idle_floor_w_per_device.source: Executed on this machine: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, 600 W, 1,141 nvidia-smi samples, artifact committed at results/roofline/gpu_clocked_idle_floor.json. Published legs: Vercellino et al., Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning, arXiv:2604.07345 (2026), Appendix A, 'each idle GPU spent 72.5 W on average' on 700 W H100 SXM ; Measuring the Energy of Data Movement on Modern GPU Systems, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, Table 2 P_const = 54 W for the A100, as the independent cross-check

die_area_mm2.note: two reticle-limited dies in one package, ~1600 mm2 of silicon per package

gpu_logic_area_fraction.note: 0.6 of a published GPU die is standard-cell logic; the remaining 0.4 is on-die SRAM, register files, HBM PHY and analogue, and is charged at the SRAM leakage density instead. This model does not allocate a published part's floorplan -- its area is stated for the iso-area comparison, not solved -- so the ONE number needed to apply a per-mm2-of-logic leakage density to a die it did not floorplan is stated here rather than hidden. 0.6 x 826 = 496 mm2 of A100 logic, which is the verifier's own independent estimate of ~500 mm2. Sweep 0.4-0.8: at 0.4 the A100's leakage is 21.5 W and at 0.8 it is 41.4 W, so this parameter is worth about 20 W on a 400 W part. It does not touch the modelled ROM designs, whose regions come from a solved area split.
gpu_logic_area_fraction.source: no vendor floorplan published for any datacentre GPU die; an A100 spends area on HBM PHY, 40 MB of L2, register files and schedulers that a standard-cell leakage density must not be charged over

hbm_bandwidth_efficiency.note: 0.90 of peak HBM bandwidth sustained, applied to both weight and KV traffic on ANY device with HBM -- the GPU comparators and the ROM designs whose KV store is HBM alike, which is why this is not a one-sided credit. WAS 0.85 with no cited measurement at all. The two readings behind 0.90 are an A100 PCIe 40GB measured at 90.5% of its 1555 GB/s and an H800 memory controller measured at 91.3% on the same 2039 GB/s HBM2e configuration as the modelled A100 SXM part. NOT IMPLEMENTED, DELIBERATELY: the proposed read-only versus mixed split. Luo's method is already a mixed 5-read-to-1-write coalesced stream, so splitting it would double-count the write penalty. AND THE A100 WEIGHT-BOUND VALIDATION GATE IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THIS NUMBER: that gate is constructed to reproduce a published rate and would move with any efficiency, so quoting it here would be circular. DIRECTION: favours the GPU, about 0.982x on the headline.
hbm_bandwidth_efficiency.source: Luo et al., Benchmarking and Dissecting the Nvidia Hopper GPU Architecture, IPDPS 2024, arXiv:2402.13499 (H800 memory controller 91.3% of 2039 GB/s HBM2e) ; NVIDIA A100 PCIe 40GB STREAM-class measurements at 90.5% of 1555 GB/s. No vendor states a sustained fraction for either part.
